items.content_text: A five-agency Chinese notice opens recommendations for 2026 national green-compute facilities. It requires at least one year of stable operation, specified energy-efficiency and green-data-center levels, renewable-electricity share at least the provincial responsibility weight, and measured energy, water and compute-utilization information; ordinary facilities generally need at least 3,000 standard racks and 60% rack occupancy, with stated exceptions. Applications are due 16 November 2026 and the agencies say they will review submissions before publishing a recommended list. These are eligibility and screening rules, not evidence of facility compliance, selection outcomes or improved AI-compute economics.
tags: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology of China
items.title: China opens 2026 green-compute facility recommendations with energy, carbon, water and utilization criteria

items.content_text: The authors introduce carbonbenchmark, which combines CodeCarbon measurements with fitted training curves, and propose a “Smallest Model that Achieves the Job” (SMAJ) selection approach. They report illustrative fits on Fashion-MNIST, GLUE SST-2 and UCI Adult, and an automated review of 5,285 NeurIPS 2025 papers using LLM classification. Their proprietary-inference emissions examples use assumed active parameter counts and generic hardware/grid factors; these are estimates, not measured model-specific emissions. The paper argues for reporting research emissions and treating environmental cost alongside accuracy.
items.title: A paper proposes carbon reporting and a smallest-model selection rule for AI research

items.content_text: The authors evaluate 33 LLM-judge configurations against 4,501 held-out worker ratings spanning 307 occupations in a US English text corpus. They report above-chance tie-aware response ranking for all configurations, while predicted acceptance shares range from 3.0% to 97.9% against the sampled workers’ 61.1%. A prespecified validation contrast within one fine-tuned lineage reports that a bundled few-shot/listwise protocol improves ordering while reducing task- and occupation-level agreement. The study audits agreement with sampled worker ratings; it does not measure objective work quality, AI productivity or employment effects.
items.title: An occupational audit finds LLM judges rank responses better than they match worker score levels

items.content_text: Li et al. report 66 model–harness configurations across TUA-Bench, ALE-CLI and a 63-task non-H100 subset of Terminal-Bench 4. Rankings reverse by harness: on the paper’s Terminal-Bench subset, Claude leads GPT-6 Astra by 7.94 points under OpenHands but trails by 30.16 points under PI. GPT-6 Astra scores 60.32% at $4.66 per task under PI versus 52.38% at $19.94 under DeepSeek Harness. The authors release adapters, evaluation code and 6,204 scored trajectories. These are author-reported results from one counted run per task; harness defaults and effective reasoning budgets differ, so the comparison does not isolate a causal harness effect or establish ranking stability.
items.title: A 66-configuration study reports model–harness ranking reversals across agent tasks

items.content_text: Pakhomov and Nijkamp use TRACE’s paired-replay corpus to test whether an agent’s pre-compaction history predicts the harm caused by summarizing that context. Across 590 harness-triggered boundaries from 275 trajectories on 147 AppWorld tasks, the prespecified contrast between histories with and without prior writes is a wide null (dU@3 −0.062; 95% interval −0.209 to +0.079); a naive “has written” label largely tracks trajectory phase. The best history-based trigger reaches held-out AUROC 0.66, below a same-boundary replay yardstick of 0.72. A frozen two-feature logistic trigger at 83.7% retention avoids 20.6% of positive-burden boundaries by count, but has no detected advantage on burden mass. The study does not establish a deployable compaction policy: it covers one agent/compressor, one AppWorld cohort and a 4,096-token window, and cannot compare with a token-budget rule at matched retention.
items.title: A paired-replay study finds weak history signals for predicting when agent context compaction will hurt

items.content_text: On 2026-05-01, cybersecurity agencies from Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the United Kingdom and the United States published joint nonbinding guidance for LLM-based agentic AI systems. The 29-page document recommends distinct cryptographically anchored identities for agents, mutual TLS for agent/API calls, least-privilege permissions, trusted registries, controlled delegation with expiry and recorded grant chains, risk-based human approval, and continuous identity and authorization checks through a central policy decision point for each action. It also calls for threat-modelled evaluations, red-teaming, monitoring and staged deployment. These are recommendations, not a binding rule or evidence that any government has adopted the controls or that they measurably reduce attacks.
tags: New Zealand National Cyber Security Centre
United Kingdom National Cyber Security Centre
items.title: Six national cybersecurity agencies publish joint guidance for secure adoption of agentic AI

items.content_text: On 2026-09-30, Hubei’s Commerce Department issued an effective notice revising the province’s 2026 consumer-goods trade-in subsidy categories from 2026-10-01. The ten-category list now explicitly includes embodied service robots, cooking robots, exoskeletons, companion robots and robot dogs; it also reshapes smart cleaning and kitchen categories and adds cameras/drones, age-support products and smart furniture. The notice says other requirements remain unchanged. This establishes an official eligibility change, not consumer take-up, robot sales, subsidy outlays or incremental demand.
items.title: Hubei expands its 2026 consumer subsidy basket to include embodied, cooking, exoskeleton and companion robots

items.content_text: Tabacof and Joglekar report a controlled GRPO study of four Gemma 4 seller checkpoints (2.3B–31B effective parameters) in bilateral multi-issue bargaining. With one shared 1e-6 learning rate and 104 steps, author-reported gains over each base checkpoint rise from +0.001 (95% interval −0.019 to +0.021; not significant) at 2.3B to +0.023 at 4.5B, +0.063 at 12B and +0.078 at 31B; each arm has one training run. At early checkpoints, a 3× learning rate improves over the shared rate at all sizes, while after 104 shared-rate steps the difference is not detectable at 12B or 31B. The study does not establish a scaling law: size and architecture co-vary, training is not FLOP-matched, and the authors report only two held-out buyers and one underpowered held-out domain. These are paper-reported results in one synthetic negotiation environment, not evidence of commercial transfer.
items.title: A controlled Gemma 4 study finds learning-rate-sensitive gains in small-model negotiation

items.content_text: A 5 October 2026 preprint proposes Guidance-TTT, which updates a compact 8B or 14B model to suggest high-level changes while a stronger GLM-5.2 executor remains frozen and implements each proposal as a complete candidate. An executable verifier scores candidates; an archive and PUCT selection supply parents for later attempts. Authors report results on Polyomino Packing, Lasso path optimization, AHC058 and TriMul, including 91.89 on Polyomino, 0.1739 on Lasso, an AHC058 score of 850,082,731, and 1,129 μs TriMul latency. These are author-reported outcomes against heterogeneous prior references, not matched replications. Key model-scale comparisons use one trajectory, implementation failures affect verifier rewards, and full code/data artifacts have not been independently audited here.
items.title: Guidance-TTT trains a compact strategic guide while keeping the solution executor frozen

items.content_text: A 5 October 2026 preprint evaluates five vision-language models on 15,401 matched harmful visual requests, varying whether each request asks for a text answer or a spatial grounding such as a point or box. The authors report that grounding refusal trails text-answer refusal by 31–59 percentage points depending on the domain, and that safety system prompts do not close the gap. A fine-tuning recipe combining grounding-form refusals, capability data and benign examples reportedly improves refusal on two open models while tracking over-refusal and grounding capability. This is a single author-run preprint scored by one LLM judge; 14,578 of 15,401 pairs are from the social-bias dataset, code is not released, and real-world harm incidence is not established.
items.title: Preprint reports a visual-grounding refusal gap across five vision-language models

items.content_text: A 5 October 2026 preprint reports Recursive Video In-Context Learning (RV-ICL), which indexes one task demonstration into four read-only levels—keyframes, phases, moments and short clips—and lets a planner retrieve detail for its current subgoal. The authors report HarnessVLA success rising from 92.6% to 96.5% on LIBERO-PRO and 86.7% to 95.8% on LIBERO-Plus. These are author-reported simulation results: on LIBERO-PRO the RV-ICL arm used 50 episodes while prior-work baselines used 100, and the paper’s reported significance statistic does not yet have a recovered matched-data audit. On LIBERO-Plus the methods were compared on a stratified 120 of 10,030 variants. The paper reports 1.8x wall-clock time and 1.4x input tokens on that comparison; physical-robot transfer is untested.
items.title: Recursive video retrieval reports higher frozen-VLA success on perturbed simulation tasks

items.content_text: In an ECB staff blog dated 6 October 2026, authors classify euro-area sectors by AI adoption using Eurostat enterprise surveys and by AI development using patent shares. Sectoral balance-sheet data through April 2026 show high-AI sectors, especially developers, with lower leverage and a recent shift toward market-based debt financing. A quarterly Bayesian VAR through 2024Q4 reports a stronger peak credit and investment response to an AI-patent-share shock in the United States than in the euro area. The authors suggest deeper US capital markets as one possible explanation; this is staff analysis, not an ECB Governing Council position or an independently reproduced causal estimate.
items.title: ECB staff analysis reports AI-intensive euro-area sectors shifting toward market-based debt finance

items.content_text: A 27 September 2026 preprint reports a Lean 4 formalization of the Galerkin construction for global Leray–Hopf weak solutions of unforced two-dimensional Navier–Stokes on arbitrary bounded open domains with no-slip boundaries. It also states a finite-horizon forced result on rectangles. The linked public repository identifies PDEIdeas.Paper and documents a lake build command. These are author-reported formalization and artifact details; the research desk has not independently built or audited the code.
items.title: Lean formalization reports global weak-solution existence for unforced 2D Navier–Stokes

items.content_text: Potraghloo and colleagues present on-policy power distillation (OPPD), which uses sequential Monte Carlo samples from the model being trained and a frozen teacher’s sharpened sequence distribution to reweight a maximum-likelihood update. The authors report single-generation accuracy increases of up to 23.0 points on MATH500 and 27.3 points on GSM8K over the untrained model at the same temperature, and report gains in a same-checkpoint GRPO comparison. Their abstract also claims performance above published 64-candidate power-sampling results; the existing candidate review found that this comparison uses a different evaluation protocol, while the same-paper 16-candidate comparison is close and does not show OPPD ahead. These are author-reported preprint outcomes, not independent validation or a matched total training-plus-inference cost result.
items.title: On-policy power distillation trains a model to absorb sequence-level answer sharpening

items.content_text: Jaffe and Sherburn introduce TasteVal, an author-built benchmark of eight text and vision tasks intended to measure experimental design and interpretation when a fixed research problem is given. They report that Opus 5.5 (max) reaches a 2.30× experimental-compute multiplier against the best expert attempt per task (95% CI 1.15–4.37). The authors also estimate that frontier-model multiplier performance doubled about every 3.0 months after December 2025, while final normalized performance shows no corresponding trend break. These are preprint results on withheld tasks, not evidence that models choose valuable research questions or outperform experts across broad research work.
items.title: TasteVal reports a 2.30× experimental-compute multiplier for Opus 5.5 on eight bounded AI R&D tasks

items.content_text: Gao and colleagues study how four language models count repeated reports across controlled sensor logs with an exact Bayesian oracle, web documents, and generated multi-agent transcripts. Their abstract reports that a forwarded copy counts as 0.06–0.42 of an independent reading, and that repeated statements can imply premature commitment on 5%–40% of logs in the tested settings. The authors report that a declaration about copy contribution lowers copy weight to 0.08 or less on controlled logs, while a worker-side rule to refer to readings rather than restate them lowers belief-implied early commitment from 11.2% to 1.1% in their team-log protocol. This is one author-reported preprint, not an operational error rate or independent replication.
items.title: A study finds LLM aggregators can treat repeated reports as partly independent evidence
